data.title: New checkout A/B test
data.question: Does the new checkout increase the conversion rate?

decision_rule.metric: conversion lift, treatment minus control (percentage points)

plan.question: Does the new checkout increase the conversion rate?
plan.estimand: Difference in conversion probability between the new and the old checkout, treatment minus control, in percentage points, over checkout sessions of genuine customers in the 14-day experiment window.

decision_rule.metric: conversion lift, treatment minus control (percentage points)

columns.name: session_id
columns.note: unique id of the checkout session; one row per session

columns.name: user_id
columns.note: id of the user; a user has 1 to 4 sessions and the variant is assigned per user

columns.name: day
columns.note: day of the 14-day experiment, integers 0 to 13

columns.name: variant
columns.note: experiment arm, exactly 'treatment' or 'control'; the estimand is treatment minus control

columns.name: platform
columns.note: platform of the session: web, ios or android

columns.name: is_internal
columns.note: True for sessions of internal staff or test users, who are not genuine customers

columns.name: session_seconds
columns.note: session length in seconds; very short sessions are bot-like

columns.note: 1 if the session ended in a purchase, else 0; the outcome

steps.title: Internal traffic
steps.description: Decide whether employee and QA test sessions (is_internal) stay in the analysis population.

options.label: Keep all sessions
options.rationale: The experiment was randomised over every visitor, so analysing everyone is the pre-registered intent-to-treat population.

options.label: Exclude internal accounts
options.rationale: Employee and QA sessions place test orders, are not customers and are not covered by the question. Their share is unbalanced across arms, so they can create a lift the checkout did not cause.
options.spec: Drop rows where is_internal is true.
options.source: Kohavi, Tang & Xu (2020), Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, Cambridge UP, ch. 3 and 21 (filter internal traffic and bots)

steps.title: Bot filter
steps.description: Decide whether sessions too short to be human are removed.

options.label: No bot filter
options.rationale: Bots are assigned at random like everyone else, so they only dilute both arms equally and the difference stays unbiased.

options.label: Drop sessions under 2 seconds
options.rationale: Sessions shorter than two seconds cannot complete a checkout and are the usual signature of automated traffic; removing them sharpens the denominator.
options.source: IAB/MRC Invalid Traffic Detection and Filtration Guidelines Addendum (2020); ABC bot-filtering guidance

steps.title: Novelty window
steps.description: Decide whether the first days, when users react to novelty, count.

options.label: Use all 14 days
options.rationale: Using the full window keeps the pre-registered sample size and avoids a post-hoc choice of cut-off.

options.label: Drop days 0-2
options.rationale: A new interface attracts curiosity clicks that fade within days, so early days overstate the steady-state effect. Dropping the ramp-up estimates the lasting effect.
options.source: Hohnhold, O'Brien & Tang (2015), Focusing on the Long-term, KDD; Kohavi, Tang & Xu (2020), Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments, Cambridge UP, ch. 3 (novelty and primacy effects)

steps.title: Unit of analysis
steps.description: Variants are assigned per user, but users return up to four times: decide whether the unit is the session or the user.

options.label: All sessions
options.rationale: Conversion rate is defined per session by the product team, and every session is an opportunity to buy.

options.label: First session per user
options.rationale: Randomisation is by user, so repeated sessions of the same user are not independent. One row per user matches the randomisation unit and removes within-user dependence.
options.spec: Keep the earliest session (by day, then session_id) of each user.
options.source: Deng, Lu & Litz (2017), Trustworthy Analysis of Online A/B Tests, WSDM

steps.title: Statistical model
steps.description: Estimate the conversion lift and its uncertainty.

options.label: Two-proportion z-test
options.rationale: The textbook test for a randomised binary outcome; it needs no model assumptions beyond large samples.
options.spec: Lift in percentage points, treatment minus control, with a normal-approximation 95% CI and a two-sided pooled z-test p-value.

options.label: Logistic regression with platform
options.rationale: Adjusting for a prognostic covariate such as platform improves precision without biasing a randomised comparison.
options.spec: Logit of converted on treatment and C(platform); the treatment effect is the average marginal effect in percentage points, with its delta-method CI and p-value.
options.source: Lin (2013), Agnostic notes on regression adjustments, Annals of Applied Statistics

data.reason: Employee and QA sessions are test traffic outside the customer population the question is about; removing them is the standard first check of an online experiment.
A checkout cannot be completed in under two seconds, so such sessions are automated traffic; the threshold is a convention that deserves one sentence of justification.
Novelty effects fade over the first days of a new interface, so dropping them estimates the steady state; the cut-off is a judgement but the practice is recognised.
Randomisation is by user, so analysing one row per user respects the unit of randomisation; it narrows the sessions counted but not the question.
Adjusting a randomised comparison for a prognostic covariate improves precision and keeps the same estimand.

steps.title: Statistical model
steps.description: Estimate the conversion lift and its uncertainty.

options.label: Two-proportion z-test
options.rationale: The textbook test for a randomised binary outcome; it needs no model assumptions beyond large samples.
options.spec: Lift in percentage points, treatment minus control, with a normal-approximation 95% CI and a two-sided pooled z-test p-value.
options.code:
import math

import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats


def estimate(df, ctx):
    treated = df.loc[df["variant"] == "treatment", "converted"]
    control = df.loc[df["variant"] == "control", "converted"]
    n_t, n_c = len(treated), len(control)
    p_t, p_c = float(treated.mean()), float(control.mean())
    diff = p_t - p_c
    se = math.sqrt(p_t * (1 - p_t) / n_t + p_c * (1 - p_c) / n_c)
    pooled = (treated.sum() + control.sum()) / (n_t + n_c)
    se_null = math.sqrt(pooled * (1 - pooled) * (1 / n_t + 1 / n_c))
    p_value = 2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(diff) / se_null))
    z = stats.norm.ppf(0.975)
    return {
        "estimate": diff,
        "ci_low": (diff - z * se),
        "ci_high": (diff + z * se),
        "p_value": float(p_value),
        "n": int(n_t + n_c),
        "extra": {"rate_treatment": 100 * p_t, "rate_control": 100 * p_c},
    }

options.label: Logistic regression with platform
options.rationale: Adjusting for a prognostic covariate such as platform improves precision without biasing a randomised comparison.
options.spec: Logit of converted on treatment and C(platform); the treatment effect is the average marginal effect in percentage points, with its delta-method CI and p-value.
options.source: Lin (2013), Agnostic notes on regression adjustments, Annals of Applied Statistics
options.code:
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf


def estimate(df, ctx):
    data = df.assign(treatment=(df["variant"] == "treatment").astype(int))
    fit = smf.logit("converted ~ treatment + C(platform)", data=data).fit(disp=False)
    margins = fit.get_margeff(at="overall", method="dydx", dummy=True).summary_frame()
    row = margins.loc["treatment"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(row["dy/dx"]),
        "ci_low": float(row["Conf. Int. Low"]),
        "ci_high": float(row["Cont. Int. Hi."]),
        "p_value": float(row["Pr(>|z|)"]),
        "n": int(fit.nobs),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["treatment"])},
    }

option.label: Linear probability model, SEs clustered by user
option.rationale: Variants are assigned per user and users return several times, so session rows are correlated; standard errors that ignore this are too small. A user-clustered estimator is the standard correction.
option.spec: OLS of converted on treatment with cluster-robust standard errors grouped by user_id; report the coefficient in percentage points, its CI and p-value.
option.source: Abadie, Athey, Imbens & Wooldridge (2023), When Should You Adjust Standard Errors for Clustering?, QJE

option.label: Keep only engaged sessions (30 seconds or more)
option.rationale: Short sessions are low-intent browsing, so restricting to engaged sessions isolates users who actually considered buying.

data.reason: Clustering by the randomisation unit is a recognised correction when users contribute several sessions; it changes uncertainty, not the population.
Engagement is measured after exposure to the variant, so conditioning on it changes the population and can bias the comparison; not a bot filter.

report.robustness_design_note: uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 10 distinct results; independent of the beam search
report.narrative: The default analysis reports a conversion lift of +0.53 pp (95% CI +0.14 to +0.92, p = 0.008) across 29,926 sessions, which clears the rule and says SHIP. The minimal flip changes Internal traffic from "Keep all sessions" to "Exclude internal accounts". That lift does not survive one defensible decision. 339 sessions come from internal accounts (employees and QA), 76% of them landed in the treatment arm, and 59% of them converted because they were test orders. Excluding internal accounts leaves 29,587 sessions and a lift of -0.14 pp (95% CI -0.50 to +0.21, p = 0.434), which says DON'T SHIP. This is the single decision that moves the estimate most (0.67 pp); the next largest, 0.26 pp, leaves the verdict unchanged.
caveats: Robustness headline is design-weighted (60%): uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 10 distinct results; independent of the beam search. The share among the explored universes is 67%, but the beam search samples the universes that are closest to flipping, so that figure leans toward flips.
Influence is measured by switching one decision at a time from the defaults; it is a statement about this analysis, not a causal claim about the world.
The no-effect reading rests on the 339 flagged sessions being test traffic; confirm the is_internal flag with the data owner.
Excluding internal accounts does not prove the new checkout has no effect, only that the data cannot distinguish it from zero.
